moonshot._note:
EXCEPTION (verified 2026-08-04): glm-5.2 and kimi-k3 are NOT in the synced table at all — checked against all 2,391 cached entries and every upstream id. Absent from sync AND absent here means every install records them as UNPRICED, which is a live capture leak on the two newest models. So they ARE curated, each carrying the vendor's own pricing URL in _source. That is the opposite of the hand-typed glm-5 stub this note warns about: that one was INVENTED, these are published and cited.
  OPERATOR-PINNED (2026-09-02): these actively-used z.ai / Moonshot models stay curated so EVERY install (fresh / CI / isolated test home) prices them without waiting for `sync-prices` to have run there — even once sync carries them (e.g. glm-5.3 is in sync yet pinned here on purpose). A pinned rate OVERRIDES sync, so the standing obligation is to keep each pinned entry current with its cited source whenever the vendor revises rates.

zai._note:
z.ai / Zhipu GLM and Moonshot Kimi carry NO curated rates on purpose: the synced breadth layer (`spendguard sync-prices`, refreshed daily) publishes real per-1M rates for the whole zai/* and moonshot/* families, and pricing.price() now resolves a bare id (glm-4.6, kimi-k2.5) against them. A curated entry here would OVERRIDE that live data — which is exactly how a hand-typed glm-5.2 STUB (0.6/2.2) came to under-price the real z.ai 5-series (1.0/3.2) by ~40%. Add an entry here ONLY with a verified source URL + date; otherwise an unpriced id fails LOUD, which is the correct accounting behavior.
  EXCEPTION (verified 2026-08-04): glm-5.2 and kimi-k3 are NOT in the synced table at all — checked against all 2,391 cached entries and every upstream id. Absent from sync AND absent here means every install records them as UNPRICED, which is a live capture leak on the two newest models. So they ARE curated, each carrying the vendor's own pricing URL in _source. That is the opposite of the hand-typed glm-5 stub this note warns about: that one was INVENTED, these are published and cited.
  OPERATOR-PINNED (2026-09-02): these actively-used z.ai / Moonshot models stay curated so EVERY install (fresh / CI / isolated test home) prices them without waiting for `sync-prices` to have run there — even once sync carries them (e.g. glm-5.3 is in sync yet pinned here on purpose). A pinned rate OVERRIDES sync, so the standing obligation is to keep each pinned entry current with its cited source whenever the vendor revises rates.
